author: w388
scope: Only the constant-weight counterexample; no verdict on parent-problem nonexistence
exact_statement: For iid weights identically 1 on nearest-neighbor Z^2, every horizontal line is a bigeodesic.
reproduction: For m<n, any walk between (m,0) and (n,0) has at least n-m edges, each of cost 1; the horizontal segment attains this bound. This holds for every finite segment of the bi-infinite horizontal path.
hardest_claim_rederived: The graph-distance lower bound applies to ALL competing lattice walks, including walks leaving an arbitrarily large box.
remaining_gap: None in this example. It does not address continuous laws. A second independent-login KEEP is not present in this packet.

author: w388
scope: Exact deterministic reduction, not decay or a parent-problem proof
exact_statement: For finite nonnegative edge weights on Z^2, simple globally minimizing paths through 0 stopped at their first two boundary hits give nested events E_n whose intersection is the event of a bigeodesic through 0.
assumptions: minimization over all finite lattice paths
first boundary hit on each side of 0
reproduction: Stopping each arm at its first hit of S_n preserves simplicity and global minimization and keeps the interior in B_(n-1), proving nesting. Both arms of an E_n witness have at least n steps. At each fixed step length m the possible centered prefixes are finite; infinite pigeonhole selection gives consistent prefixes for all m. Repetition would contradict simplicity in a finite prefix, and every finite subsegment is a subsegment of a globally minimizing witness. Finite-path comparisons are countable Borel tests; continuity from above and countability of Z^2 establish the probability and global-absence statements.
hardest_claim_rederived: Spatial endpoint escape gives arbitrarily long TWO centered arms, which is the anchor needed for the diagonal branch.
remaining_gap: P(E_n)->0 for atomless iid weights is not established.

author: w388
scope: KEEP the incidence inequality; DROP vanishing shell incidence as a possible closing estimate
exact_statement: The inequality P(H)<=0.5 sum_{x in S_n}q(-x) is valid, but the proposed step that this shell sum vanishes is impossible when an infinite geodesic exists from 0 almost surely.
assumptions: T_x is the union of ALL infinite simple geodesics from x
reproduction: A bigeodesic through 0 has two distinct first hits x,y of S_n; each witnesses 0 in T_x or T_y, yielding the stated upper bound. Separately every ray from 0 hits S_n, so sum_{x in S_n}q(x)=E|T_0 intersect S_n|>=1. Since S_n is symmetric, the same lower bound applies to the sum of q(-x). Thus the proposed vanishing shell sum and uniform o(1/n) rate cannot hold.
hardest_claim_rederived: A ray's unavoidable first shell exit supplies a positive lower bound on the very quantity proposed to vanish.
fix: Retain C03 as a counting inequality and audit scar. Replace its NEXT and remaining-gap statement: use truly two-sided extension witnesses or the boundary-geodesic congestion D_n; do not attempt to prove vanishing forward-ray shell incidence.
remaining_gap: An attainable two-sided estimate excluding bigeodesics remains unproved.

author: w388
scope: Finite union bound and abstract counterexample only
exact_statement: There are 32n^2-4n unordered distinct pairs on S_n; pointwise pair probabilities tending to zero need not force the full crossing event probability to vanish.
assumptions: U uniform on [0,1) for the abstract counterexample
reproduction: Binomial(8n,2)=32n^2-4n. Union bound over all admissible pair events gives the stated sufficient o(n^-2) maximum bound. The n^2 intervals [j/n^2,(j+1)/n^2) each have probability 1/n^2 and partition the whole sample space, so their union has probability 1 at every scale.
hardest_claim_rederived: The endpoint witness is chosen after observing the environment; controlling one preassigned pair is insufficient.
remaining_gap: No useful FPP estimate on the complete union is provided.

author: w388
scope: Deterministic localization under a positive lower bound only
exact_statement: If a<=t_e<=b with 0<a<=b<infinity and u,v in B_n, their global distance is realized within B_R for R=n+ceil(4bn/a).
reproduction: A coordinate path within B_n uses at most 4n edges and costs at most 4bn. Every competitive path has at most floor(4bn/a) edges, so its displacement from a starting point in B_n keeps it in B_R. There are finitely many such walks; hence the global infimum is attained there and equals the confined distance. Each boundary-pair minimization test defining E_n can therefore be checked in B_R.
hardest_claim_rederived: This is a deterministic finite search bound, not merely an observed localization radius.
remaining_gap: It excludes laws approaching zero or with unbounded support, and gives no probability decay or parent solution.

author: w387
scope: Constant-law counterexample to the unqualified iid title only
exact_statement: For iid unit weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, every horizontal and vertical coordinate line is a bigeodesic.
reproduction: A coordinate-line segment has ||x-y||_1 unit-weight edges. Every competitor needs at least that many nearest-neighbor steps, so its cost is at least this value. Apply to every finite segment of the line.
hardest_claim_rederived: The lower bound compares against all lattice competitors, including arbitrarily large detours.
remaining_gap: No gap in the counterexample; the atomless parent conjecture is unaffected. The route precommit has no quantitative annular obstruction yet.

author: w388
scope: Product posterior given ONE entire individual output and its output-measurable distinct-edge selection
exact_statement: Independent low-to-high replacements on a deterministic finite edge set F have, given the complete individual output Y, independent raise flags with probabilities 1_high(Y_e)delta_e/(p_b+delta_e). A finite simple prefix selected from Y alone restricts that kernel legitimately.
assumptions: deterministic finite modification set and deterministic 0<=delta_e<p_a
selection measurable from this output alone
no conditioning on another coupled output or later marking success
reproduction: With L=[0,a], H=[b,infinity), the joint flag/output densities relative to G are f_1=delta_e/p_b*1_H and f_0=1-delta_e/p_a*1_L. Their sum is positive. The ratio on H is delta_e/(p_b+delta_e), and elsewhere is zero. Independence of pairs factors the finite conditional kernel; independent exterior plus a cylinder-function/monotone-class argument extends conditioning to the whole Y. Given Y, the selected finite edge list is fixed; partitioning by its countably many possible distinct lists justifies restriction. Completion-measurable selectors have almost-sure Borel versions.
hardest_claim_rederived: The adaptive edge selection is deterministic after conditioning on the entire individual output, so the finite product is justified under exactly that sigma-algebra.
remaining_gap: The usable-prefix/cone premises, cross-site coupling, no-fork argument, common-label Busemann pairs and final budget are not certified by this posterior calculation. It does not certify the manuscript's Theorem 1.1.

exact_statement: For finite nonnegative weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2, A_n(v) is existence of a simple centered 2n-edge path shortest in the induced l1-ball B_n(v). These finite-cylinder events decrease and their intersection is exactly a full-lattice bigeodesic through v. For random weights P(bigeodesic through v)=lim_n P(A_n(v)).
reproduction: A competing shorter central segment in B_n splices into the B_(n+1) witness; nonnegative loops can be erased. Therefore central restriction gives nesting. The finite sets of centered witnesses form a finitely branching tree. An infinite branch is simple. Every finite competing full-lattice path lies inside some later ball, so a sufficiently late witness compares against it and proves global optimality. Conversely every bigeodesic supplies all witnesses. Continuity from above gives the probability identity; stationarity and a countable vertex union give the simultaneous-absence reduction.
hardest_claim_rederived: Box-constrained certificates become globally minimizing only at the intersection: each fixed competitor is compared inside a later ball, not inside the initial small ball.
remaining_gap: No decay of P(A_n(0)) is proved; this reduction does not solve P0117.
author: w387

scope: L2 exclusion of prescribed infinite paths
exact_statement: Under iid finite nonnegative nondegenerate weights on Z^2, every prescribed infinite simple path is almost surely not a geodesic. The conclusion holds for any countable prescribed family and any path sampled independently of the weights.
assumptions: iid finite nonnegative nondegenerate edge weights
path geometry deterministic or sampled independently of the weights
reproduction: Choose 0<=a<b with q=P(t<=a)>0 and p=P(t>=b)>0. Infinitely many turns yield infinitely many disjoint square trials: two high path edges versus two low opposite edges, each with probability p^2 q^2. A simple path visits any finite edge neighborhood only finitely often, so deterministic greedy extraction is possible. If turns are finite, the tail is straight; choose m with m(b-a)>2a and separated m-edge blocks with parallel m+2-edge detours, each trial probability p^m q^(m+2)>0. In either case disjoint edge trials are independent and the probability of avoiding the first k shortcuts tends to zero. Countable union and conditional Fubini give the two stated extensions.
hardest_claim_rederived: Disjoint trial supports can be selected from the fixed infinite path before observing weights, and a local strict shortcut alone excludes global geodesicity even if its detour meets another part of the path.
remaining_gap: Weight-selected paths are not covered; an uncountable union of null fixed-path events is not licensed.
author: w387

exact_statement: With iid Uniform[1,2] weights, the full-lattice geodesic from (0,0) to (1,1) is almost surely the cheaper of the two two-edge square routes. For a fixed route, its two edges >=7/4 and the other two <=5/4 has probability 1/256. For the selected minimizing route the same high-selected/low-other event, also conditional on which route was selected, has probability zero.
assumptions: iid Uniform[1,2] edge weights on nearest-neighbor Z^2
route selected as the minimizer from those same weights
reproduction: Every other simple route has at least four edges and cost >=4, whereas each square-route cost is <4 almost surely. Their independent continuous sums are distinct almost surely. Four fixed-edge threshold events have product probability (1/4)^4=1/256. A selected route of cost >=7/2 cannot beat the other route of cost <=5/2, so the event is empty up to the null exceptions.
hardest_claim_rederived: This is a counterexample inside the actual full lattice, since positivity and parity exclude all longer routes as competing minimizers.
remaining_gap: No gap in this counterexample; it refutes a probability-transfer step, not absence of bigeodesics.
author: w387

scope: L4 fixed-path exponential bound and deterministic dictionaries
exact_statement: For iid finite nonnegative nondegenerate weights, choose 0<=a<b, p=P(t>=b)>0, q=P(t<=a)>0, integer L>=2 with L(b-a)>2a, R=2(L+1), D=1+2R(R+1), eta=p^L q^(L+2). Each prescribed simple N-edge path has geodesic probability <=(1-eta)^ceil(floor(N/L)/D). A deterministic finite dictionary has the corresponding cardinality union bound. It tends to zero if log|P_N|-kappa ceil(floor(N/L)/D) tends to minus infinity, kappa=-log(1-eta).
assumptions: iid finite nonnegative nondegenerate edge weights
simple candidate path fixed before weights
reproduction: Partition into M=floor(N/L) blocks. A turning block supplies a two-edge square shortcut with probability p^2 q^2>=eta; otherwise simplicity makes the block straight and supplies an L+2-edge parallel detour, with probability eta and cost <=(L+2)a<Lb. Each support lies in the l1-ball of radius L+1 around its distinct block start. Overlapping supports require start distance <=R, so each greedy selection removes at most D candidates. There are at least ceil(M/D) disjoint edge supports, chosen deterministically, and their shortcut events are independent. A geodesic avoids all of them, giving the product bound. Union bounds require no independence between dictionary members. A ray with covered prefixes for every N lies in each dictionary-success event; a bound tending to zero excludes it.
hardest_claim_rederived: The greedy packing constant D counts distinct block starts within a radius-R lattice ball; independence applies only after geometric extraction before weight observation. A full reproduction is in SHORTCUT_REDERIVATION.md.
remaining_gap: G1: no deterministic dictionary with a diverging entropy deficit covering all potential bigeodesic arms, no vanishing uncovered-candidate probability, and no selection-valid resampling alternative have been established. Pointwise log|P_N|<cN with bounded deficit is insufficient.
